data.body:
MEASUREMENT REFINED — the silent class is ~5 assertions, not 255, and a GREEN SUITE IS EVIDENCE OF THE
BUG rather than evidence against it.

## The 255 figure was the wrong denominator

Splitting the 255 `caplog` occurrences by what they do when zero records arrive:

    NEGATIVE assertions — PASS VACUOUSLY when void (the severe class):        5
      tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py:147  assert not any("zeroed/implausible" in r.message ...)
      tests/unit/test_usage_log.py:254               assert not caplog.records
      tests/unit/test_config_default_assignee.py:75  assert not any("default_assignee" in r.message ...)
      tests/unit/test_config_llm.py:197              assert not any("llm" in r.getMessage().lower() ...)
      (plus one further match)

    POSITIVE assertions — FAIL LOUDLY when void:                             25
      `assert any(... caplog ...)` raises AssertionError; `next(... caplog ...)` raises StopIteration.

The remaining occurrences are setup, `caplog.at_level(...)` and similar, not assertions.

So the coverage-integrity problem — an assertion that verifies nothing while reporting success — is
about FIVE assertions. The other 25 are a FLAKINESS problem: they announce themselves by going red, as
one of them did. Auditing all 255 would waste the effort; auditing these 5 is a bounded job. This
supersedes the "54 files / 255 occurrences" search space in the description above.

## A GREEN SUITE DOES NOT MEAN THE POISONING DIDN'T HAPPEN

A full default-selection run on CLEAN main at 6cdd4b00d passed: 9219 passed, exit 0. That is NOT
evidence the mechanism is absent — the mechanism was proven directly on that same clean tree
(`configure_logging()` flips `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` True -> False and never restores
it).

The two observations are consistent, and the reason is the whole point of this ticket: if the
poisoning occurred in that run, the five negative assertions would have PASSED VACUOUSLY and the run
would still be green. The only reason anyone noticed at all is that ONE victim happened to use
`next(...)`, which raises on an empty iterator instead of quietly succeeding.

That is the sharpest available statement of the defect: WE CANNOT TELL, FROM A GREEN RUN, WHETHER THOSE
FIVE ASSERTIONS VERIFIED ANYTHING. Determining it requires instrumentation, not inspection of the
result.

## Consequence for the acceptance criteria

The first AC (establish how many assertions are currently void) should be scoped to these five and
answered by INSTRUMENTATION — e.g. record, per test, whether `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` was
True at assertion time and whether any records were captured. Counting from a green run cannot answer
it, because green is exactly what a void assertion produces.
